premises.text: Texting apps struggle to integrate voice effectively
premises.evidence_span: Texting apps have tried to add voice, for instance, Siri and iMessage, but if you've ever used it, you know that you could spend more time correcting mistakes than if you just typed in the first place.

premises.text: Voice applications are unusable in certain situations
premises.evidence_span: Voice applications are great if you're in the car or driving, but if you're in a meeting or in class, they're basically unusable.

premises.text: Talks integrates text and voice into every message
premises.evidence_span: Instead of choosing whether I'm going to send text or voice, talks incorporates text and voice into every message.

premises.text: Talks allows users to communicate on social networks easily
premises.evidence_span: Talks allows you to communicate on social networks with your people as easily as it is to send a message to one of your friends.

premises.text: Talks supports multiple media formats including pictures, voice, video, doodles, music, and location
premises.evidence_span: What started off as a simple concept of putting text and voice into every message evolved into a fully featured messaging app that supports pictures, voice, video, doodles, music, and location.

premises.text: Talks can send messages to anyone regardless of their device or app
premises.evidence_span: Talks doesn't require the receiver to have the app. So I can send messages literally to anyone, no matter what device they have or what apps they have.
So we created a technology called voice cloning. Over time, it learns your voice when you speak to the app, and it creates a voice clone of you on the cloud.

value.text: Talks enhances communication by integrating text and voice in a user-friendly way
value.evidence_span: you won't have to choose whether you type or talk or read or listen, because talks always has both formats in every message.

notes: No external knowledge applied; all claims are based on the transcript.
